proposal.summary: The ashmem kernel driver fails to enforce its protection mask when storing the backing shmem file in a VMA, allowing an attacker to use remap_file_pages() to regain VM_MAYWRITE and then mprotect() to obtain write access to an ashmem allocation's backing file. The driver also allows marking pages purgable even for read-only ashmem fds, effectively zeroing them.
proposal.affected_product: ashmem kernel driver on Linux (upstream master) and Android (observed on Pixel 2, security patch level 2019-09-05)
proposal.cwe_quote: However, it improperly stores the backing shmem file, whose ->mmap() handler does not enforce the same restrictions, in ->vm_file.

AV.quote: An attacker can abuse this through the remap_file_pages() syscall

AC.quote: An attacker can abuse this through the remap_file_pages() syscall

PR.quote: An attacker can abuse this through the remap_file_pages() syscall

I.quote: allows an attacker to gain write access to the ashmem allocation's backing file via mprotect().

A.quote: there is no access control for these - even if you only have read-only access to an ashmem file, you can still mark pages in it as purgable, causing them to effectively be zeroed

proposal.recommended_next_step: Investigate and produce a kernel patch that prevents storing the backing shmem file in vma->vm_file without enforcing ashmem's prot_mask (or ensure shmem->mmap enforces the same restrictions). Also consider mitigating remap_file_pages() use on ashmem mappings (e.g. deny or validate remap) and add a unit test reproducer; backport to supported Android kernels.

evidence_quotes.claim: ashmem stores backing file in vm_file without enforcing same restrictions
evidence_quotes.quote: However, it improperly stores the backing shmem file, whose ->mmap() handler does not enforce the same restrictions, in ->vm_file.

evidence_quotes.claim: attack path uses remap_file_pages to regain VM_MAYWRITE
evidence_quotes.quote: An attacker can abuse this through the remap_file_pages() syscall, which grabs the file pointer of an existing VMA and calls its ->mmap() handler to create a new VMA.

evidence_quotes.claim: successful result is gaining write access via mprotect
evidence_quotes.quote: In effect, calling remap_file_pages(addr, size, 0, 0, 0) on an ashmem mapping allows an attacker to raise the VM_MAYWRITE bit, allowing the attacker to gain write access to the ashmem allocation's backing file via mprotect().

evidence_quotes.claim: purge API can zero pages even for read-only fd
evidence_quotes.quote: there is no access control for these - even if you only have read-only access to an ashmem file, you can still mark pages in it as purgable, causing them to effectively be zeroed
